goals.name: Workers Comp Process Improvements — On-Site Incident Workflow + Compliance
goals.assessment: First real engagement with this goal all quarter (8/26). Anne's problem statement: injuries currently surface after the fact via the WC carrier, not proactively; a 3-day gray period where movers self-manage soreness-vs-injury at home produces zero visibility; branch managers are being migrated out of the reporting/admin chain in favor of EE owning it directly. Recommendations discussed, none decided or built yet: (1) decouple 'report the incident' (mandatory, same-day, no-penalty) from 'is it a real injury' (assessed after); (2) two structured EE touchpoints during the gray period instead of silence; (3) split who physically responds on-site (still BM/lead — unavoidable) from who owns the paperwork (fully EE); (4) a 24/7 nurse triage line (Concentra, already used for the HPE) to solve after-hours clinic-or-not calls by phone instead of a manager driving to a job site; (5) automate the old paper-packet idea as an auto-sent one-pager the moment an incident is reported; (6) sequence tooling light-to-heavy — Monday form or text line first to prove the reporting-behavior change, custom app only after that's proven. Nothing built or committed to yet — this is still the strategy conversation, not implementation.
blockers: No decisions locked yet — recommendations discussed 8/26, not yet chosen from or approved by Anne
Tool choice (Monday form vs. text line vs. custom Rippling app) not yet made
Nurse triage line vendor relationship (Concentra or otherwise) not yet explored for after-hours WC use, only for the HPE
goals.green: Custom Rippling claim-submission app live, built against the OSHA-recordable field spec handed to Matisen before the data structure locks, with a working EE-notification loop confirmed, plus the on-site incident workflow documented and trained to all 10 BMs, by Sept 15.
goals.superGreen: Green + mover-specific WC training delivered as a Back to School module + a test OSHA-formatted export produced from Q3 data + one real Q3 WC leave case showing correctly in Rippling leave-tracking.

goals.name: Implement Weekly Start/Stop/Keep Conversations — Scaling Up Practice
goals.assessment: ⚠️ 8/26 correction (Cameron + Anne): the goal was misread earlier the same day. What got built and shared with the other 6 Roundtable leaders' COS agents (a manager-to-own-direct-reports weekly checklist, Rippling-roster-pulled) is NOT the actual design. Real goal, per Cameron 8/26: one weekly Start/Stop/Keep conversation, rotating through the 7 Roundtable leaders one at a time, each paired with a randomly assigned NON-leader employee from anywhere in the company (deliberately cross-functional/cross-geography — e.g. Brian↔a Philippines CX teammate, Amanda↔a DFW mover) to keep leadership connected to the front line broadly, not just their own chain. Middle managers don't run these conversations — they own acting on the feedback that surfaces. The mismatched pattern was retracted on the SCB thread same day (told the other 6 agents to hold off building). Anne + Cameron are aligning further tomorrow (8/27); rebuild starts after that conversation, not before.

Decision #18 (damages attribution) resolved — Cameron + Paul's compromise (team/job-level governs bonus + gates, individual fault stays coaching-only) with six amendments closing the design gaps. New Decision #19 locked (no grandfathering on launch). The HQ itself got a major upgrade: ladder table restructured into paired Standard/Fast Track columns and made interactively editable, two new tabs added (Decision History, How It Works — plain-language mechanics for BMs and movers), and a full visual restyle to match the mover-pay-premium page's look. Revised 8/21: Paul pushed back on Decision #18's attorney-confirm framing (no attorney gate needed — TX right-to-work, damages can stand alone as a termination reason for gross negligence or a documented pattern); Anne agreed same day. 8/25: three more rounds of direct decisions from Anne — fast-track performance bars set as provisional working numbers (9/9/10/10), Master Lead's standard bar lowered 9.5→9.0, Lead General's Master-Lead fast-track hours locked at 1,365, HOF decided as purely honorary (not a job title), Decision #16 fully closed out (PTL hours don't carry into Senior Lead's hour count), and a real table-structure bug found and fixed (Master Lead/Lead General row data had been swapped). Two of today's calls reverse positions Paul was explicit about on 8/20 (bar values, look-back window) — heads-up posted to the rock pulse, his reply pending.
